findings.title: The reviewed security architecture is entirely proposed and the supplied baseline still contains exploitable SUPER_USER privilege paths

sourceEvidence.explanation: Every unrecognized role, including SUPER_USER, is normalized to STUDENT instead of an unauthorized role.
Roles other than STUDENT, PROFESSOR, or TEACHER enter the final all-courses institute branch, effectively treating SUPER_USER and unknown roles as Admin-like readers.
Non-Admin authorization trusts persisted permission JSON and has no hard SUPER_USER or unknown-role ceiling.
Any authenticated actor can retrieve join code, instructor email, syllabus metadata, assessment points, and announcement content without course relationship, institute, or role authorization.

findings.impact: An active SUPER_USER can currently inherit student, Admin-like, or injected legacy permissions and access data outside the dedicated oversight DTO. Unknown stored roles can receive the same unintended rights. The proposed new policy modules and route guards do not exist in the supplied baseline, so the exposure remains live at source level.
findings.recommendation: Before implementation approval, retain AF-01/AF-02 as blocking findings and require the plan to implement a fail-closed recognized-role resolver, a hard SUPER_USER legacy ceiling independent of persisted permissions, and direct guards on every inventoried handler/action/service. Verify wrong-role denial before parsing, protected lookups, side effects, and external execution.

findings.title: Authentication-only mutation and execution boundaries allow SUPER_USER side effects before the proposed ceiling exists

sourceEvidence.explanation: All mutations require only requireWorkspaceSession; no role or course-authority check prevents SUPER_USER schedule creation, editing, or deletion.
Any authenticated user can create a course announcement for an arbitrary courseId.
Any authenticated actor can create or update a submission under its own user ID without requiring STUDENT role or approved enrollment.
Eligibility is institute-only; an ICS SUPER_USER can reach template creation, submission, activity-session, gamification, badge, and grade-passback writes.
The institute-only eligibility result is checked before Judge0 execution, but actor role is not restricted; an ICS SUPER_USER can invoke the executor.
The separate Judge0 endpoint also uses institute-only eligibility and can invoke external or fallback execution for SUPER_USER.

findings.impact: SUPER_USER can mutate schedules, announcements, submissions, grades, gamification, assessment state, and invoke external/local execution. Denial after validation or lookup would also violate the required ordering and may leak resource existence or consume rate-limit state.
findings.recommendation: Implement the shared actor-capability guard at every real handler and service entry, including aliased and sibling execution routes. The guard must run immediately after real authentication and before body parsing, rate-limit writes, resource reads, template creation, notifications, revalidation, database mutation, or external/local execution.

findings.title: Several normal-role handlers lack persisted ownership and institute-scope checks, so the proposed generic role ceiling is insufficient

sourceEvidence.explanation: An instructor alias or Admin can notify any user by supplied studentId; no course assignment, enrollment, institute, or student-role relationship is verified.
Role checking is followed by lookup of any activity submission; no persisted course assignment or institute relationship is required before deletion, grade changes, notifications, or invalidation.
An instructor alias may award EXP to any existing user and may supply an unrelated courseId without assignment or institute checks.
Role checks do not constrain supplied courseId or ruleId to the authenticated instructor's assigned courses or institute.
PROFESSOR or ADMIN can export the gradebook for any supplied courseId; the handler performs no ownership or institute check before calling the sensitive service.

findings.impact: Hardening only SUPER_USER would leave cross-course and cross-institute instructor IDOR paths and could regress AC-008 by preserving unsafe behavior rather than legitimate scoped behavior. These paths expose or mutate grades, student identities, notifications, and gamification state.
findings.recommendation: Define explicit per-operation normal-role policy: instructor alias plus assigned course plus institute, student plus approved enrollment plus owned child record, and separately adjudicated Admin scope. Resolve child IDs through the authorized parent predicate and enforce the same checks in callable services.

findings.title: Authenticated GitHub boundaries expose external repositories and accept writes without course, cohort, or ownership authority

sourceEvidence.explanation: Any authenticated user can proxy arbitrary owner/repo/path requests using that user's token; no approved repository link, course, or role relationship is required.
POST verifies only that repoLink exists, not that the actor may access it; GET accepts any repoLinkId and returns authors and replies without visibility or ownership enforcement.
Any authenticated actor can create repository links and postId queries are not constrained to course, institute, or cohort membership.

Any role not recognized as instructor/Admin is treated as a student and receives its own submission behavior; SUPER_USER is not explicitly denied, while instructor reads lack course ownership and institute checks.

findings.impact: A SUPER_USER could use legacy GitHub integration despite H-08, and ordinary authenticated users may enumerate or modify repository-linked data outside persisted course authority. External GitHub requests also occur on insufficient authorization.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit SUPER_USER denial and relationship-aware authorization before parsing or outbound GitHub calls. Require ownership or authorized course/cohort linkage for every repoLink, post, submission, comment, repository proxy, and CI boundary; do not trust owner/repo/path supplied by the caller when a persisted link is required.

findings.title: Knowledge Exchange eligibility inherits the unknown-to-STUDENT alias and grants SUPER_USER the entire ICS feature suite

sourceEvidence.explanation: Eligibility is determined from the home institute while role is obtained through normalizeRole; an ICS SUPER_USER becomes STUDENT and eligible. Caller headers and query parameters can deny but do not establish trustworthy selected scope.
Every eligible ICS actor can read and create posts, receive author metadata, and trigger gamification; no SUPER_USER ceiling exists.
Institute eligibility alone permits external AI execution for an ICS SUPER_USER.
Institute eligibility alone permits votes, aggregate mutations, and EXP awards.

findings.impact: SUPER_USER can read and mutate Knowledge Exchange data and invoke AI services, contrary to the approved login/logout/own-identity-only support exception and the oversight-only role ceiling.
findings.recommendation: Make Knowledge Exchange eligibility require an explicit supported legacy role, with SUPER_USER and UNKNOWN denied before request parsing, database reads, external AI calls, voting, notifications, or gamification. Preserve existing authorized-role semantics and the separate anonymous public-leaderboard decision.

findings.title: The proposed middleware pathname marker remains an unproven trust boundary for Next RSC, rewrites, and server actions

sourceEvidence.explanation: The baseline middleware neither removes a caller-provided pathname marker nor installs a server-derived marker. Static and _next requests bypass processing, and API routes receive headers only.
The selected design depends on a future overwritten server-derived pathname request marker and explicitly says to stop if its trustworthiness cannot be proven.
Marker, RSC, shell, and compiled-action tests are only proposed and marked NOT_EXECUTED; the supplementary files do not exist.

findings.impact: If the marker is absent, spoofable, dropped during RSC navigation, normalized differently, or bypassed by a rewrite/action request, the shared institute layout can serialize or render legacy children and shell widgets containing private academic data. Direct API/action guards reduce but do not eliminate page/RSC leakage.
findings.recommendation: Treat the marker mechanism as a blocking proof obligation. Specify the exact private header name, unconditional removal/overwrite behavior, canonical pathname normalization, rewrite behavior, RSC and server-action handling, and fail-closed layout behavior. Independently review and execute adversarial direct, prefetched, RSC, rewritten, encoded, and compiled-action requests. Replace the design if trusted provenance cannot be demonstrated.

findings.title: The account-support exception is not consistently reflected in the implementation allowlist and existing endpoints

sourceEvidence.explanation: Any authenticated actor, including SUPER_USER, can change its password, although H-08 permits only login, logout, and /api/auth/me.
Any authenticated actor can extend its session and obtain identity metadata; this is outside the approved exception list.
Any authenticated actor can revoke an owned session, also outside the approved exception list.
SUPER_USER can read and mutate profile fields under the baseline authentication-only policy.
These routes are modification-eligible, but the architecture does not provide endpoint-specific dispositions for anonymous password recovery versus authenticated SUPER_USER behavior.

findings.impact: Without exact endpoint dispositions, implementers may either leave prohibited account-management rights open or break anonymous password-recovery behavior. A blanket role block after parsing can also cause the wrong status or side effects.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit route-and-method support matrix. Preserve genuinely anonymous forgot/reset/register behavior as public workflows, but deny authenticated SUPER_USER access to change-password, refresh, sessions, profile, avatar, settings, notifications, GitHub OAuth, and similar account-management boundaries unless a new human decision expands H-08. Define whether authenticated credentials on an otherwise public route are ignored or denied.

findings.title: The implementation allowlist creates ambiguity around the human-resolved anonymous public leaderboard exception

sourceEvidence.explanation: This is an anonymous public route whose existing DTO includes student ID, display name or alias, avatar, points, tier, and program.

The public leaderboard is included as modification-eligible with the generic purpose 'Handler-entry role ceiling', even though it has no authenticated actor and the human decision requires unchanged public behavior.
The human explicitly excluded anonymous public leaderboard behavior from AC-007 and required its behavior and DTO/privacy semantics to remain unchanged.

findings.impact: A generic SUPER_USER ceiling cannot be meaningfully applied to an anonymous endpoint. Leaving it in the modification allowlist risks adding authentication, changing its DTO, or treating anonymous public data as a failed oversight confidentiality case, contrary to U-01.
findings.recommendation: Remove the public leaderboard from modification-eligible paths or give it an explicit no-change review-only disposition. Supplementary tests should assert unchanged anonymous behavior and separately prove that oversight responses do not internally reuse or serialize the public leaderboard DTO.

findings.title: Audit and error-failure behavior is proposed but lacks a transactional or non-serialization proof

sourceEvidence.explanation: Audit append is a separate database write and the schema/API provides no immutable or atomic read-plus-audit primitive.
AuditLog is an ordinary mutable table with String metadata and user foreign keys; immutability is not database-enforced.
The audit-failure test and adapter are future proposals, do not exist, and are NOT_EXECUTED.

findings.impact: A service may fetch sensitive DTO data, fail the audit append, and still serialize or cache data through an error, RSC payload, logging path, or caller reuse. Conversely, auditing before a successful read can create misleading ALLOWED records if projection later fails.
findings.recommendation: Specify a narrow service result that cannot expose projection data unless audit append succeeds, with no shared cache and safe error conversion at every caller. Independently review failure injection and RSC serialization behavior. Keep the lack of database immutability and denial-audit expansion explicitly documented.

findings.title: Proposed supplementary verification is neither implemented nor independently reviewed, so claimed complete boundary coverage is unsupported

sourceEvidence.explanation: Every command is marked NOT_EXECUTED; five supplementary test paths are described but do not exist.
The architecture relies on future security, alias/audit, runtime, desktop privacy, and mobile privacy suites.
Independent red-team applicability review, supplementary assertion review, fresh preflight, authoritative plan, controller provenance, and approvals remain prerequisites.

findings.impact: Role aliases, unknown roles, persisted-permission injection, Cookie/Bearer conflicts, all 120 handlers, 20 action files, callable skills, six inline actions, audit failure, RSC/shell leakage, archive/empty behavior, and normal-role regressions have no implemented or executed evidence. AC-012 is not satisfied.
findings.recommendation: Do not advance the controlled stage. Author the supplementary suites only after approval, obtain independent assertion-adequacy review and fresh exact-source preflight, execute all mapped commands through the unchanged runner, and require per-handler/export evidence without skipped loop members.

findings.title: The supplied packet does not contain source bodies for every inventoried route and server action, preventing the required independent full-scope review

sourceEvidence.explanation: The inventory declares 120 route files, 20 action files, and an additional sensitive service.
The proposed allowlist states 153 existing modification-eligible files, including actions, inline actions, layout components, and callable skills.
The design depends on review of every verb/export, including six inline actions and server-callable skills, but the sanitized source packet supplies only a subset of their bodies.

findings.impact: This review cannot independently verify every declared/aliased verb, action export, inline action, callable skill, shell component, or page guard. Treating inventory labels or proposed test names as source review would fabricate coverage.
findings.recommendation: Provide a new source-bound sanitized packet containing every one of the 120 route bodies, all 20 action files, the additional gradebook service, all shared authorization/session/eligibility modules, and relevant layouts/components, with stable line numbering. Repeat the independent review before architecture PASS.

methodsOrExportsReviewed: All 120 inventoried route rows and every declared or aliased HTTP verb were reviewed at inventory level; the aliased activities/codelab/invalidate POST was traced to codelab/instructor/reject
coverage.assessment: Inventory classification completed, but source-level completeness is not established because the packet omitted bodies for a subset of the 120 routes. Protected routes include admin, course, workspace, activity, CodeLab/Judge0, KX, GitHub, gamification, flashcard, profile/settings, notification, material, integrity, upload, leaderboard, study-session, todo, and user-profile boundaries.
Approved basic support, but SUPER_USER initial-ICS behavior requires an explicit branch because the baseline treats SUPER_USER as non-Admin and locks login to home institute.
Approved logout exception. Cookie/Bearer precedence and session selection require supplementary conflict tests.
Approved own-identity exception with no-store headers; ensure DTO remains own identity only.
Anonymous recovery workflow; must remain distinct from authenticated SUPER_USER support rights. It performs rate-limit/OTP/email writes.
Anonymous registration explicitly maps only public student/instructor roles; preserve the exclusion of SUPER_USER and ADMIN.
Anonymous OTP workflow; route-specific handling is needed so its continued public availability is not confused with a SUPER_USER account-support permission.

Public operational endpoint exposes database host, environment-variable selection, table counts, connectivity errors, and configuration hints. It is outside SUPER_USER role authority but should be separately threat-reviewed operationally.
Public institute listing is an explicit unchanged supporting route; it returns whole Institute records rather than an oversight DTO.
Human U-01 explicitly preserves anonymous behavior and DTO/privacy semantics. It should be review-only, not modified by a SUPER_USER role ceiling.

HMAC-authenticated service boundary. The sanitized body redacts the fallback value and has a sanitized hash different from the original, so the actual secret-fallback semantics cannot be independently assessed from this packet.

methodsOrExportsReviewed: All exports listed for 20 action files
coverage.assessment: Inventory-level review completed. The packet omitted the action bodies, so actual role, ownership, institute checks, validation ordering, and side effects could not be independently verified.
Inventory identifies a sensitive direct-read service, but its source body was not supplied. Caller-only protection is insufficient; service-boundary authorization remains an unverified proposal.
Unknown and SUPER_USER roles collapse to STUDENT. Proposed explicit role recognition is necessary and unimplemented.
requireAdmin remains effectively Admin-only, but requirePermission trusts persisted permissions for every non-Admin and needs a hard SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN ceiling.
Eligibility is institute-only and admits an ICS SUPER_USER to execution and submission paths.
Home-institute eligibility plus unknown-to-STUDENT normalization admits ICS SUPER_USER across KX. Caller claims can deny but are not authority.
Cookie is preferred; if absent or invalid, Bearer is tried. The helper selects one session rather than merging actors, but conflict/revocation semantics remain unexecuted.
Opaque DB sessions and inactive/expired cleanup are confirmed. Transitional raw session-id lookup remains and must be included in token-edge tests.
Baseline provides only cookie-presence redirects and response headers. The proposed trustworthy pathname marker and SUPER_USER route allowlist are absent and unproven.

No schema migration is needed for the string role. Existing relationships can support scoped predicates, but AuditLog immutability is not enforced and many sensitive child relationships require explicit authorization.
Reviewed as a proposed verification interface only; it is not implementation evidence or a passing gate.
Exact DTO and denial helpers are present, but benign markers cannot establish production semantic privacy. Human-approved empty-string amendments require separate supplementary assertions.
All executions are NOT_EXECUTED. Supplementary files are future proposals and have not received independent assertion review.
Contract validation requires structured findings, plans, and command mappings but does not convert documentary proposals into completed gates.
HIGH work requires predecessor artifacts, fresh evidence, independent reviews, and signed approvals. Current DRAFT state cannot satisfy release readiness.
A captured historical receipt does not establish present freshness; no receipt was independently verified in this session.
Confirms read-only isolated provider design and host-scoped proposal application, but no controlled stage was accepted in this preparation.

limitations: The sanitized packet did not supply source bodies for every one of the 120 route files, all 20 server-action files, six inline actions, callable skills, the gradebook exporter, or the relevant dashboard layouts/components. Inventory-level review is not a substitute for source-level coverage; REVIEW_FAIL is required.

Line numbers for minified one-line JSON and Markdown documents are necessarily reported as line 1 because the supplied representations contain the relevant artifact in a single serialized line or do not preserve source line metadata.
The GitHub webhook source was sanitized and its sanitized SHA-256 differs from the original SHA-256. The redacted fallback-secret value cannot be independently reviewed.

No commands, tests, databases, external requests, filesystem reads, source writes, provider dispatches, approvals, or controller transitions were performed. No runtime, build, test, preflight, or gate PASS is claimed.
The new academic-authorization, academic-oversight, DTO, API, page, and shell files do not exist in the supplied baseline. Their proposed behavior cannot be reviewed as implemented behavior.
The five supplementary test files do not exist and all mapped executions are NOT_EXECUTED; coverage labels and future test titles provide no passing evidence.

The human-resolved anonymous public leaderboard scope was honored: no finding asserts that its existing anonymous DTO violates AC-007. The finding concerns only allowlist ambiguity and preservation of that decision.
